entities.name: GlmU query sequence
observations: 500-aa sequence has strong homology to reviewed bacterial bifunctional GlmU proteins: 52–54% identity over about 93% query coverage.
Likely catalyzes the final two steps of de novo UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis: glucosamine-1-phosphate acetylation and GlcNAc-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase activity.
Homology-based annotations associate this function with peptidoglycan and bacterial lipid A biosynthesis.
Closest reviewed reference annotations report cytoplasmic localization and homotrimeric assembly; these are inferred for the query, not independently established.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis
observations: GlmU catalyzes the final two sequential reactions of the de novo UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthetic pathway, according to reviewed homolog annotations.

entities.name: Peptidoglycan biosynthesis
observations: UDP-GlcNAc produced by GlmU supplies a precursor for bacterial peptidoglycan biosynthesis; participation is supported by homolog annotations.

entities.name: Lipid A biosynthesis
observations: Reviewed GlmU homolog annotations link the enzyme to bacterial lipid A biosynthesis; this is an associated downstream use of UDP-GlcNAc.

entities.name: Cytoplasm
observations: Reviewed bacterial GlmU homologs are annotated as cytoplasmic; localization of the uncharacterized query is inferred from homology.
